market_rationale: Stagflationary backdrop: August CPI 3.4% headline with re-accelerating core, Brent above $100 on unresolved Iran conflict, 10y at 4.96% and 30y at 5.35%, consumer sentiment collapsing to 47.8 with inflation expectations jumping to 4.6%. Breadth is poor (equal-weight lagging SPY by 1.75% over 21 sessions, only ~23% of assets positive). The FOMC on Sept 15-16 is a binary catalyst; high rates and oil favor cap-weighted mega-cap resilience over cyclicals and small caps. Dispersion is high (oil, crypto, Korea, Brazil far from the pack) but most equity sub-groups are in shallow drawdowns rather than shock lows, so genuine reversal setups are scarce. Cybersecurity is the one candidate combining a strong prior relative trend, modest pullback, low volume stress and low beta to an oil/rates shock.
portfolio_rationale: Only cybersecurity passes the overreaction-plus-55% test: a top-ranked prior trend, shallow drawdown, benign volume, and moderate beta into a high-rate, high-oil FOMC week. Everything else on the slate is either a shock candidate with a negative multi-window trend (defense, solar, robotics, industrials), a high-beta recent winner without in-window support (semis, Taiwan, crypto), or a rate-sensitive small-cap or muni exposure facing rising yields and collapsing consumer sentiment. Given poor breadth and mega-cap resilience, SPY remains the default for the remaining slots.
